description: We are an enthusiastic group of aspiring engineers from Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM). Although we are only in our first year of pursuing a degree in Aerospace Engineering, we are eager and courageous enough to embark on this exciting journey through the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are ready to take on the challenges ahead, push ourselves beyond our comfort zones, and discover our full potential as future engineers.
summary: AgroSpace XCEL is a decision-support website built by AgroSpace XCEL, a team of first-year Aerospace Engineering students from Universiti Sains Malaysia. It helps Malaysian farmers deal with shifting rainfall, heat, water shortages and declining soil health. Users pick a location on an interactive satellite map, or click anywhere to drop a pin. They then enter their crops, soil condition and priority, such as conserving water or rebuilding soil. AgroSpace XCEL combines NASA Earth observation sources (Landsat vegetation data, SMAP soil moisture, GPM IMERG rainfall, NASA POWER climate data) with soil and weather data. From these it produces a field-health score and plain-language crop-rotation advice, such as legume breaks, cover crops and drainage planning. It will provide reasonings behind each recommendation and be transparent about uncertainty, so it never invents data for locations without verified values.
details:
Our project is represented in a website named “Agrospace Xcel”. In this website, users can analyse their field health by giving their field coordinate,intended crops,soil condition and priority. Then, the app will show the field health in a percentage form after considering several parameters based on NASA latest data such as average daily rainfall,current temperature,surface moisture and others. A simple recommendation is also given to farmers for further action.
Our website works with a method that has four stages which is observe,interpret,explain and adapt. First of all, raw data collected by NASA Earth-observation satellites provide a consistent view of conditions across a selected field. Then, a series of parameters such as rainfall, moisture, temperature and vegetation are read together rather than in isolation. As a result, a percentage score paired with the signals that influenced it will be printed out, so the result is understandable and trustable. Therefore, farmers can prioritize monitoring, irrigation, drainage or field checks as conditions shift. In a nutshell, we make Earth observation easier to understand without hiding the uncertainty or the “why” behind a recommendation.
This website is important because Malaysian farmers nowadays face huge challenges from the environment such as water shortage and declining soil health, and those will become a crucial factor when selecting their crops. Therefore, we use FieldShift as our decision-support concept in our website for exploring crop-rotation strategies that protect fields, conserve water and strengthen long-term resilience. Therefore,we hope that Malaysian farmers can use our website to make a better decision and prevent loss during extreme weather conditions.
In terms of the website structure,it was developed by using HTML5, with GitHub serving as the primary development environment, source code repository and version control platform.
The website's visual resources, including team photographs, organisational logos and other graphical elements, were organised within a dedicated assets directory. The website was subsequently deployed and published through GitHub Pages, providing public web accessibility.
The Technical Stack is listed as below:
Web Technology:HTML5
Development Platform:GitHub
Version Control: Git
Web Hosting and Deployment: GitHub Pages
Visual Assets: PNG and JPEG image formats
Our project is unique because we use a simple percentage-based indicator to represent the field health with some key parameters, which ensure everyone can utilize the website without professional knowledge. We know that there are many factors that influence the field health, but we choose four main factors which are average daily rainfall,temperature,surface moisture and vegetation. We also consider several methods to represent the field health but we eventually choose the current percentage form because it is easier for understanding.
